shippingNews.postTitle: Vessels On the Hook as Fall Storm Brings Gales

stories.body: FRIDAY 9 a.m. UPDATE: Please see the attached Boatnerd AIS images for vesels at anchor on the St. Marys River Friday morning. ORIGINAL REPORT: As a powerful fall storm system brings widespread rain and potentially hazardous winds to Michigan, with gale warnings issued for all Great Lakes waters surrounding the state, some vessels have sought shelter to wait out the storm. On the hook Thursday evening in Goulais Bay , on the Canadian side above the Soo Locks, was the Two Harbors-bound James R. Barker. Above DeTour were the saltie Charlie (with a Burns Harbor destination), Flevoborg and Indiana

Duluth-Superior Harbor Mesabi Miner departed the Superior Entry at 15:30 central Wednesday afternoon carrying iron ore pellets destined for Lake Erie Works at Nanticoke. The Duluth entry didn’t see any ship traffic until later in the day when Algoma Intrepid arrived at 19:20 and Walter J. McCarthy Jr. departed at 21:20; Intrepid arrived with salt from Goderich and McCarthy departed with iron ore pellets destined for Conneaut. todayInHistory.title: Sam Laud
todayInHistory.text: Sam Laud Bay Shipbuilding Corp. of Sturgeon Bay, WI, laid the keel for their hull # 712 on Jan. 4, 1974 to be built as a smaller-sized Great Lakes self-unloading bulk cargo carrier. The new vessel was launched on Nov. 19, 1974 for Buffalo's American Steamship Co. (ASC), a subsidiary of GATX Corp., Chicago, IL. Completed in 1975, the self-unloader was christened Sam Laud by Mrs. Edna Laud on behalf of her husband at a christening ceremony held April 15, 1975. Mr. Laud was the former president (1945) and chairman of the board (1956) of GATX Corp., having started with the company in 1916 as shop painter and riveter. Mr. Laud died August 1, 1963. GATX Corp. had acquired ASC in July of 1973. Mrs. Laud was accompanied by Mr. Frederick G. Jaicks, chairman and CEO of Inland Steel Co., Chicago, IL, who gave the address at the christening ceremonies. One of a new generation of self-unloaders for the ASC fleet, the Sam Laud was built at an approximate cost of $13.3 million and was the fourth of 10 self-unloaders launched for the fleet under Chapter XI of the Merchant Marine Act of 1970. Under this act, the U.S. government-guaranteed financing and tax deferred benefits for fleet modernizing. The other ASC self-unloaders built under this program were the Roger M. Kyes (now Adam E. Cornelius, 1973), Charles E. Wilson (now John J. Boland, 1973), H. Lee White (1974), St. Clair (1976), Belle River (now Walter J. marineWeather.synopsis: A 29.6 inch low over southern Ontario this morning lifts to southern Quebec at 29.5 inches this afternoon. In its wake, a 30.8 inch high lifting off of the Central Rockies weakens to 30.6 inches today as it moves east over the Plains. This evening, the aforementioned low deepens to 29.4 inches and heads towards the Mouth of the St. Lawrence River. The high then slides south of the Great Lakes at 30.5 inches by Saturday night as a 29.2 inch Alberta Clipper moves through the northern Canadian Prairie Provinces towards Hudson Bay, deepening to 29.1 inches by the time it arrives on Sunday. By Sunday, the high will build to 30.6 inches over the northeastern CONUS. As the low moves east over Hudson Bay and weakens with time Sunday night into Monday afternoon, expect high pressure of 30.3 inches to return to the Upper Great Lakes by late Monday. The high pressure strengthens to 30.4 inches over Lake Superior by Tuesday, then 30.5 inches over northeastern Ontario Tuesday evening and 30.6 inches over Quebec Wednesday.

AFTERNOON

marineWeather.synopsis: Low pressure of 29.7 inches over northeast IL will deepen to around 29.4 inches as it shifts into the eastern Great Lakes through today. Expect a northerly wind shift tonight to increase to high-end gales by late this morning as the low departs while a strong high pressure around 30.7 inches builds into the Plains. A Gale Warning remains in effect for all of the open waters of Lake Michigan later this morning into tonight. Light rain will continue over the north half overnight, with intermittent rain over the south half. Lake effect showers and a few thunderstorms are possible today along the back side of departing low pressure. A few waterspouts are possible in the showers/thunderstorms, particularly over the south half of Lake Michigan. As the high sinks toward the Ohio River Valley on Saturday, strong low pressure around 29.0 inches will develop in northern Manitoba through the weekend. The tight pressure gradient may bring southwest gales to Lake Michigan on Sunday, primarily over the north half.
marineWeather.warning:
GALE WARNING IN EFFECT FROM 10 AM CDT THIS MORNING THROUGH
LATE TONIGHT

marineWeather.synopsis: Deepening low pressure tracks across the central Great Lakes this morning. A strong cold front in its wake brings northerly gales this afternoon and evening. A ridge of high pressure then builds across the Ohio Valley on Saturday and Sunday with gusts westerly winds across the central lakes.
marineWeather.warning:
GALE WARNING IN EFFECT FROM 1 PM EDT THIS AFTERNOON THROUGH
LATE TONIGHT

marineWeather.synopsis: Low pressure 29.60 inches will extend a cold front through the area today, followed by high pressure 30.50 inches building late Saturday and persisting through mid-next week.

A 29.5 inch low will move across southern Ontario province this morning, then continue to move northeast across the Saint Lawrence Valley this afternoon before reaching the Canadian Maritimes by Saturday while deepening to 29.1 inches. A 30.5 inch high will then build into the Ohio Valley Saturday night before expanding across the lower Great Lakes and New England Sunday through Monday. A broad ridge of high pressure averaging 30.4 inches will remain in place across the Ohio Valley and Great Lakes much of next week.
